steps.content: You see crimson light reflecting on the water surface of this world. Two different scenes seem to overlap...

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: ...Chief... Chief...
[Slightly trembling lens]

steps.speaker: Distant Voice
steps.content: Avocados on sale! Avocados on sale! Half off only for now! Don't miss out on this great deal! Avocados on sale!

steps.speaker: Distant Voice
steps.content: Avocados on sale! Avocados on sale! Half off only for now! Don't miss out on this great deal! Avocados on sale!

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Feeling dizzy? Seems like the information from the other dimension is too overwhelming. Let me switch to the filter mode for you...
[The image stabilizes]

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Chief, are you okay? I'm Moore. Do you remember me?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: How many "permissions" have she gained?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Five permissions: visual, audio, functions, strength, narrative... she has gained them all.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: In a real game development, she would already have enough power to dominate everything in the world.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Even if we stop her, she will still use her power to return to this point in time.
In this game, everyone's fate is being manipulated, but for her, it's just a game.
It's been such a hectic day, but looking back... everything is utterly absurd.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: You seem a bit down. Back when we lost contact, what happened between you and her?
You think back for a while, then slowly start to speak.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She took me to a strange place, and said a lot of strange things... Moore, I want your opinion.
You tell Moore about the conversation with 000, about the so-called settings, discarded file, contamination, and anomalies.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Wow... "settings database"? What did she see there? I'd really like to see for myself.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Fate?
She briefly falls silent, then laughs almost inaudibly.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: ...You all like this word.
Before you get to respond, she continues.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: As a programmer, rather than believing in fate, I believe in inevitability.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Every world has its own rules. Under certain conditions, logic and causal processes determine the direction of development. People are the same; their background, education, relationships, and past experiences collectively shape their thinking and actions.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Every person and world is a vast and complex system. It self-corrects, self-expands, and continuously progresses based on new information and environmental changes.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Of these, what can be called underlying logic, or basic premises, or causal laws, or objective external environments... the inevitable results they lead to, in your terms, might be called fate.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Oops, I droned on and on about these boring things again.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Not at all. It's quite enlightening.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You say fate is inevitability. So is it unchangeable once set? Is everything we do meaningless?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: What I mean by inevitability is that for a programming system, certain inputs lead to relatively certain outputs.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: But if you want a different result, you can change the initial input data. You can also exploit system loopholes like that girl. Some simply destroy everything in the system. That's also a choice.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: See, if you just want to change fate, there are so many paths. Which one would you take, Chief?
Her words momentarily leave you at a loss for an answer.
She smiles breezily.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Any of them. For me, the most fun is learning about the system.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Gather as much information as possible, understand its mechanisms. Once I fully grasp its logic... isn't the outcome whatever I choose?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: You are in this quandary because you don't truly understand her, right?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm in this quandary exactly because I don't understand her at all.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What she wants, what she's afraid of, what she plans to do... I have no idea.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: In other words, as long as I take the initiative to understand her and the world, there are still many things I can do.
Moore smiles as you pull yourself together.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Right on. That's the Chief I've heard about.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: That girl is indeed interesting. She's so clingy, yet there are still many things she hasn't told you. Keep interacting with her to gather info. You'll eventually understand her.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: If it's really too much of a hassle... I can always help you kill her.
[The positive atmosphere instantly drops to freezing point.]

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Of course. According to my analysis, it's entirely feasible.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: The greater her actions and threats, the more the underlying structure is exposed... making it easier to target and strike.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I'd readily take on the request. It's very challenging, but I'd do it for you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Instead of killing her...

steps.speaker: Choice
options: I'd prefer to completely subdue her.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Oh, sorry, I misunderstood. It seems Chief can't bear to let that girl die.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...No, it's not that. Her abilities are very special. Whether it's dealing with DisCity's dark web or future enemies, she'd be very useful.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Though I don't believe in predetermined fate, you're right. Everything has its rules, and information is key.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If this world can indeed observe and record our development in some way...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then I will need her help.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Hehe, I understand. This task is more complex. We need to neutralize her threats while protecting her from being rejected by the world...

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: That's fine, I'll get it done. Since it's your request, I'll ensure her safety until she's by your side.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: But next, I need someone in that world to distract her to buy me more time. Chief, can you help me with that?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're right. No matter how erratic and crazy she is, she must have her own internal logic.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: By the way, since you can track all her information, can you send her a message?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Of course. But what do you plan to do?

steps.speaker: Choice
options: I want to invite her... to play a game.
